stem:
Sameer must compute $\dfrac{3}{4} \div \dfrac{2}{5}$.

Which two claims correctly carry out the division?

options.text: Keep $\dfrac{3}{4}$ and multiply by $\dfrac{2}{5}$ directly, with no reciprocal of the divisor.
Replace the divisor $\dfrac{2}{5}$ by its reciprocal $\dfrac{5}{2}$, then multiply $\dfrac{3}{4} \times \dfrac{5}{2}$.
Say the reciprocal $\dfrac{5}{2}$ is what creates the original divisor $\dfrac{2}{5}$.

teacher.key_rationale: Dividing by 2/5 means multiplying by 5/2, giving 15/8. Skipping the reciprocal omits the required step. Saying the reciprocal creates the divisor reverses the relation.
